root_idea.summary: A root principle of solidity or firmness combined with extension and length.
root_idea.development: The physical base appears in firm elevated ground, the back and its solid paired flesh, and the hard or central parts of objects. It extends figuratively to strength, making something strong, strenuous distance, and other forms of firmness or extension.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized adjective citation form مَتِين.

senses.definition: Strong and firm; possessing strength or firmness to a high degree.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally for a firm quality or thing, and substantivized with the definite article in the divine epithet “the Strong.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or render something strong, stout, firm, or hard.
To season a skin with rob, or inspissated juice.
The back, especially the firm fleshy portions alongside the backbone; the erector-spinae region.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The paired form مَتْنَانِ or مَتْنَتَانِ denotes the two sides or portions of the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The broad side or middle portion of a sword blade, including its raised central ridge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific term for the blade’s broad central surface or ridge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hard outer or apparent part of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general term for a thing’s hard, visible exterior.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle of a bow or spear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Denotes the central section of the implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part between two poles of a house or tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A structural term for the span between the poles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Elevated, level, or plain ground; especially hard elevated ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions vary between elevated plain ground and hard elevated terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One of the four bright stars in Pegasus, specifically the star at the extremity of the neck.
A transmitted tradition or report, especially one attributed to Muhammad or one of his Companions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical or scholarly term equivalent to a hadith, report, or transmitted account.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The threads or strings of tents.
To become strong or acquire firmness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive development into the quality expressed by مَتِين.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike someone on the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The back-oriented construction may specify striking with a whip.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel through or spend the whole day in movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from traversing an extended span.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go far or travel a long, strenuous distance; to extend or separate to the utmost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also describes a journey that is severe and far-reaching.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To delay or procrastinate with someone.
To engage in a poetic exchange, with each of two poets composing a verse in turn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of poets extending a contest toward an intended end.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slit an animal’s scrotum and extract its testicle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare veterinary usage explicitly reported as exceptional.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Back and paired back-flesh sense represented.
More specific description of the paired back portions.
Sword-blade surface and ridge sense represented.
Middle of bow or spear represented.
Strong and firm adjective sense represented in the Quranic form.
Tent-string sense represented; the derivational notation adds no separate lexical meaning.

cautions: The three Quran occurrences form one QAC nominal group, tagged as two nouns and one adjective; the public headword is normalized to مَتِين, with the substantivized use retained in its usage conditions.
